thread:
samir: heads-up — customer 'acme-prod' reporting lots of 400s from /v1/embeddings when sending bulk batches. ~1200 items, only ~20 succeeded.

samir: runtime error snippet: `vector validation error: expected shape (N,1536) got (1,)` — request_id=rn_2026-03-15_18:12:43

samir: pasted their request body; looks suspiciously double-encoded:

samir: ```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-001",
  "input": "[[0.12, 0.03, ...]]"
}
```

liz: that quoted inner array is the tell — their client stringified vectors before batching. often happens with custom logging wrappers or old SDK code.

liz: did they use fetch/axios? can we see headers? if content-type != application/json or they JSON.stringify twice, server sees a string.

samir: headers show `content-type: application/json`. they admitted their wrapper calls `JSON.stringify` on each record for logs, then the batch code does `JSON.stringify(payload)` again.

derek: quick repro in node: this breaks it

```js
const vector = [0.12, 0.03, 0.5];
fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'text-embed-001', input: JSON.stringify(vector) })
});
```

derek: server receives `"[0.12,0.03,0.5]"` (string) instead of `[0.12,0.03,0.5]`. validation treats it as a scalar and fails the (N,1536) shape check.

derek: fix for clients is to NOT stringify inner vectors. correct payload: `body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'text-embed-001', input: vector })`.

samir: customer also mixes single-item vs batched calls. sometimes they send `input: "[... ]"` for single calls and `input: [[...]]` for batches. our batching layer expects consistent element types (array vs string) so mixing causes intermittent failures and throughput drops.

liz: suggestion for SDK: normalize — coerce single vector to [vector] on send, and reject elements that are strings with a clear error. that will avoid silent double-encode traps.

jordan: can we make our 400 clearer? e.g., `400 Bad Request — received stringified inner array for embeddings input; expected array[number] or array[array[number]]`. would cut down support back-and-forth.

derek: short-term mitigation idea: when we detect an element that's a JSON string, run a lightweight JSON.parse; if it parses to an array of numbers, accept it and add warning header `X-Embed-Warn: stringified-inner-array`. log for metrics so we can see prevalence.

support-bot: ticket #INC-2248 created; customer case linked. assigned to eng-runtime for validation changes if approved.

samir: sent quick repro and patch suggestion to customer repo, they will test the fix (remove inner stringify) today.

liz: also reminded them to check NDJSON/gzip streaming boundaries — if they stream newline-delimited JSON but the gzipping wrapper mangles boundaries, only the first line might be parsed. rare but seen in other cases.

samir: logs for request_id rn_2026-03-15_18:12:43 saved to /var/logs/embeddings/2026-03-15/rn_2026-03-15_18:12:43.log for trace.

jordan: I'll follow up with eng-runtime about improving client-facing 400s and adding the lightweight-parse fallback. will report back next week. :+1:

samir: closing once customer confirms their wrapper change. thanks everyone!
